Package index

Prevalence weighting

Re-price an evaluation sample to a target landscape prevalence.

reweight()
Prevalence case weights

Reported diagnostics

The two per-sample summary scores a model reports. ROC-AUC is prevalence-invariant but inflated by easy absences; PR-AUC is the recommended anchor for curve reconstruction.

roc_auc()
ROC-AUC via the rank (Mann-Whitney) identity
pr_auc()
Reported precision-recall AUC (average precision) at the sample prevalence

Average precision & PR curves

Precision-recall at a target prevalence, by the exact point-level route and the equal-variance binormal (summary-metric) route.

ap_pointwise()
Exact per-point average precision (PR-AUC) at a target prevalence
ap_binormal()
Average precision of an equal-variance binormal ROC at a prevalence
ap_scalar_to_prev()
Correct a scalar PR-AUC from its design prevalence to a target prevalence
pr_curve_exact()
Exact precision-recall curve at a target prevalence
pr_curve_binormal()
Reconstructed precision-recall curve from a binormal ROC at a prevalence

Net benefit (decision curves)

Decision-curve net benefit and its reference strategies.

nb_exact()
Net benefit of thresholded predictions at a target prevalence
nb_exact_ci()
Bootstrap confidence band for the exact net-benefit curve
nb_binormal()
Best-achievable net benefit from an equal-variance binormal ROC
nb_binormal_band()
Plausibility band for a binormal net-benefit curve from PR-AUC uncertainty
nb_treat_all()
Net benefit of the treat-all (survey-everything) reference strategy

Calibration

Assess and shift the calibration of held-out predictions.

cox_calibration()
Cox calibration intercept and slope on held-out predictions
recalibrate_to_prevalence()
Recalibrate predicted probabilities to a target prevalence (logit shift)
clamp()
Clamp probabilities away from 0 and 1

Survey-unit delineation

Turn a predicted suitability surface into mapped survey units end to end (watershed patches, subdivided and attributed). The low-level stages are internal; this is the single entry point.

survey_units()
Delineate survey units end to end

Patch ranking (RankIndex)

Prioritise candidate patches by combining rescaled terms. The network engine routes travel on roads/trails to score accessibility (A) and, on the same graph, complementarity (C) — whether a day’s work can be assembled nearby.

rank_index()
Combine the RankIndex terms into a priority score
network
Accessibility (A) and complementarity (C) on a road/trail network graph
accessibility()
Accessibility of patches over the network (A)
complementarity()
Complementarity of patches: can a day's work be assembled nearby? (C)
contract_network()
Contract an OSM network to junction-to-junction edges
osm_speeds
Default per-highway travel speeds (km/h)

RankIndex — distance terms (Dg, Dr, A)

Isotropic, terra-native distance surfaces: straight-line distance from known populations (Dg), least-cost resistance distance (Dr) over a friction surface, and Tobler walking cost for accessibility.

cost
Dispersal and accessibility terms (Dg, Dr, A) by isotropic cost distance
geo_distance()
Geographic distance from known populations (Dg)
cost_distance()
Resistance / accessibility distance by isotropic cost distance (Dr, A)
build_resistance()
Build an isotropic resistance (friction) surface
tobler_friction()
Tobler walking-cost friction for accessibility (A)
cluster_region_extents()
Cluster sources into buffered, cell-capped regions for tiled cost distance

RankIndex — survey intensity (S)

The survey-effort “bias surface” as a gridless Gaussian field of target-group occurrences, with inverse-frequency species weighting corrected for domain clipping; inverted it gives survey sparsity, where undocumented populations may hide.

survey
Survey-intensity surface (the S term) as a continuous Gaussian field
survey_surface()
Build the survey-intensity surface in one call
survey_weights()
Inverse-frequency species weights, corrected for domain clipping
guess_record_type()
Guess record type from a dataset / origin column
